title: Plumbing Scheduling Software: 6 Tools and What They Cost
html:
Plumbing scheduling software should put every call, tech and invoice on one calendar. Start with a job app that books, dispatches and invoices, then add a plumbing CRM automation layer once missed follow-ups cost you jobs. Published plans in this guide run from $29 to $533 a month. Three of the six vendors do not publish a price at all.

Plumbing scheduling software has to solve one problem: a tech in the wrong place at the wrong time. A burst pipe call at 7 a.m. collides with a water heater install booked last week. A paper calendar or a shared text thread cannot sort that out. This guide compares six tools by shop size, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Plumbing is an urgent trade. Many callers phone two or three shops, and the one that books a tech first usually gets the job. So scheduling is a revenue tool, not just an office chore.

Which plumbing scheduling software suits a one-van shop?

Jobber and Housecall Pro are the two apps a solo plumber or two-truck shop compares first. Both cover booking, scheduling, estimates, invoices and payments.

The practical split is team size. Jobber Core is built around one user, so a second tech adds a full seat. Housecall Pro Essentials bundles five users and adds GPS tracking, which helps once a dispatcher needs to see which van is closest.

Watch the fine print on price. Jobber lists three billing options, so the same Core plan can cost $29, $39 or $49 a month depending on commitment. Housecall Pro lists annual and monthly prices. Always compare like for like before you pick a winner.

Both vendors offer trials, and Housecall Pro lists 14 days with no credit card. Run a real week of calls through the trial instead of a demo job. If a tech cannot reschedule a visit from a phone in under a minute, move on.

Which plumbing dispatch software fits a growing crew?

Service Fusion and Workiz suit shops with three or more techs, where a dispatcher assigns jobs and the owner wants reports. They price differently, which matters when you hire.

  • Service Fusion: customer management, estimates, scheduling, dispatching, invoicing and payment processing. Starter is $208 a month billed annually or $245 billed monthly, with unlimited users on every plan, and plans are month to month. Limit: add-ons such as GPS fleet tracking are listed without prices.
  • Workiz: scheduling, jobs, estimates, invoices, online payments, client management and QuickBooks integration. Plans are Standard, Pro and Ultimate, each listed as request pricing. Limit: Standard allows 5 automations, Pro 10 and Ultimate 30, and phone and answering add-ons are sold separately.

Service Fusion removes the per-seat math. A shop that adds three techs in a busy season pays the same plan price, so the cost is predictable. Workiz hides its price behind a quote, so ask what a five-tech shop pays before you start a trial.

Automations matter more than they sound. A rule that texts a customer when a tech is on the way saves a dispatcher a dozen calls a day. Count how many rules you need, then compare that number with each plan limit.

Which field service platforms run large plumbing fleets?

FieldEdge and ServiceTitan are built for plumbing and HVAC companies with many techs, service agreements and a back office. Neither publishes a price.

  • FieldEdge: scheduling and dispatching, quotes, service agreements, reports and prospect tracking. Its Select, Premier and Elite plans include 2, 4 and 6 mobile app licenses. Limit: every price is request pricing, and Select has only basic dispatching and no prospect tracking.
  • ServiceTitan: a field service platform with Starter, Essentials and The Works plans. The vendor states that its per-technician pricing is designed to fit your business and goals. Limit: no price is published, so you cannot budget without a sales call.

These platforms pay off when you run service agreements and recurring maintenance across many techs. They are a poor fit for a three-truck shop. A rule of thumb: if no one on staff does dispatch full time, a lighter app costs less and gets used more.

Ask three questions on any sales call. What is the per-tech price, what does onboarding cost, and what is the contract length? Write the answers down so you can compare them with the published plans above.

How do the six plumbing scheduling tools compare?

The table puts the published facts side by side so you can see where each tool starts and where it stops.

ToolPublished entry priceUsersMain limit
Jobber$29 a month billed annually, $49 with no commitment1 on CoreExtra users cost $29 a month
Housecall Pro$59 a month billed annually1 on BasicMonthly billing costs more
Service Fusion$208 a month billed annuallyUnlimitedAdd-on prices not shown
WorkizRequest pricingNot shown5 automations on Standard
FieldEdgeRequest pricing2 app licenses on SelectBasic dispatching on Select
ServiceTitanRequest pricingPer technicianNo published price

Source: the vendor's published prices, read in November 2026. Prices exclude tax and card processing fees.

Read the table by shop size. One to two vans point to Jobber or Housecall Pro. Three to eight techs point to Service Fusion or Workiz. A fleet with service agreements points to FieldEdge or ServiceTitan.

What should a plumber test during a scheduling app trial?

Test the moments that cost you money: an emergency call, a reschedule and a missed invoice. A trial that only shows a clean demo job tells you nothing.

  1. Book an emergency call. Time how long it takes to create the customer, pick a tech and send the arrival text.
  2. Move a job. Drag a visit to another tech and another day, then check that the customer is told.
  3. Quote from a phone. Build a flat-rate estimate in the truck and send it before you leave the driveway.
  4. Close the loop. Turn the job into an invoice, take a card payment and see where the money lands.
  5. Pull one report. Look for jobs by tech and unpaid invoices, since those two answers run a small shop.

Give the trial to a tech, not just the owner. The person in the truck finds the clumsy screens first. If your best tech hates the app after three days, the schedule will fall out of date within a month.

Import a real customer list during the trial. A messy list reveals how well the app handles duplicates, multiple service addresses and landlords with many properties.

What does a plumbing software stack cost per month?

A small plumbing stack costs between $29 and $149 a month for the job app, using only the published prices above. Add the extras that fit your shop.

  • One-van shop: Jobber Core at $29 a month billed annually, plus a free Google Business Profile. Adding a second tech adds $29 a month, which makes two users $58.
  • Five-tech shop: Housecall Pro Essentials is $149 a month billed annually and covers five users. Service Fusion Starter is $208 a month billed annually and covers unlimited users.
  • Large fleet: FieldEdge and ServiceTitan are priced by quote, so budget after you collect written offers from both.

These figures cover the job app only. Card processing, a phone number add-on and review tools sit on top, and your website still needs a home.

Plan for the cost of switching, too. Moving customer records, price books and recurring visits to a new app takes real hours. Pick a tool you can live with for two years, so the price you see today is not a trap later.

Compare the stack with one average service call. If a tool costs less than a single call each month and saves an hour a day, it pays for itself. If it costs more than a week of calls, shrink the plan.

What does plumbing scheduling software not do?

Scheduling software does not bring in calls. It runs the work after the phone rings, so a full calendar still depends on search, maps and reviews.

  • Google Business Profile: the free listing that puts your plumbing company on Google Maps. Google states that creating a Business Profile and listing your business is free. Limit: it needs fresh photos and review replies to rank near the top.

A site that books jobs matters as much as a calendar. A web form that drops straight into your scheduling app saves a dispatcher the retyping.

How do you choose plumbing scheduling software?

Choose plumbing scheduling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: can a tech reschedule from a phone, and does the customer get an arrival text? Does it price by flat rate or by line item?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, add-ons and card fees, then compare the total with one average service call.

Setup effort: can one person import customers, build a price list and train techs in a single week?

A one-van shop can run on Jobber Core, a free Google Business Profile and a simple site. A five-tech shop with a dispatcher fits Service Fusion or Housecall Pro Essentials. A fleet with maintenance agreements should price FieldEdge and ServiceTitan against each other.

Software does not create demand. Pair it with lead sources. Search ads from Google Ads for plumbers and Google Local Services Ads put a phone call on the calendar.

What is the best scheduling software for a small plumbing company?

There is no single best, because it depends on crew size. For one to two vans, Jobber Core at $29 a month billed annually or Housecall Pro Basic at $59 are common starts. For three or more techs, Service Fusion offers unlimited users. Test each on a real week of calls.

How much does plumbing scheduling software cost?

Published plans in this guide run from $29 a month for Jobber Core, billed annually, to $533 a month for Service Fusion Pro, billed annually. Workiz, FieldEdge and ServiceTitan do not publish prices. Card processing fees and add-ons cost extra, so ask each vendor for a total.

Do plumbers need dispatch software or just a calendar?

A calendar works for one van with a few jobs a day. Dispatch software starts to pay off when a second tech joins and jobs change during the day. It shows who is free, sends arrival texts and keeps invoices tied to each visit.

Is there free plumbing scheduling software?

The vendors in this guide sell paid plans, though most offer a trial. Housecall Pro lists a 14 day trial with no credit card, and Workiz lists 7 days. A shared Google Calendar is free but lacks invoicing and customer history, so it fits only a very small shop.

Can plumbing scheduling software bring in new customers?

No. Scheduling software organizes work after a customer calls. New calls come from search, maps, reviews and ads. A free Google Business Profile, a fast website and paid search put your number in front of homeowners before you schedule anyone.

When should a plumbing company move to a bigger platform?

Move up when you manage service agreements, several dispatchers or many techs, and your current app cannot report on them. Until then a lighter tool is cheaper and easier to learn. Request pricing from FieldEdge or ServiceTitan only when those needs are real.

Can plumbing scheduling software bring in new customers?
No. Scheduling software organizes work after a customer calls. New calls come from search, maps, reviews and ads. A free Google Business Profile, a fast website and paid search put your number in front of homeowners before you schedule anyone.
###
When should a plumbing company move to a bigger platform?
Move up when you manage service agreements, several dispatchers or many techs, and your current app cannot report on them. Until then a lighter tool is cheaper and easier to learn. Request pricing from FieldEdge or ServiceTitan only when those needs are real.
